scope: Starter content; no real appointments, adopted policies, or contacts are created

champions.title: Find your department Copilot champion
champions.intro: Champions help colleagues choose safe prompts, learn everyday workflows, and share feedback. They do not replace the service desk, approve access, or handle sensitive incidents. Select your department in the directory below. Appointed profiles can include a short summary and an approved profile-photo link. If its status is Not assigned, ask the CoE program owner to nominate a champion; no person or contact is implied by the sample rows.

sampleRows.expertise: Lesson planning and accessible teaching materials
Non-sensitive service guidance and communication drafts
Troubleshooting, safe use, and support escalation
Approved policy summaries and generic onboarding

champions.maintenance: The directory owner confirms primary and backup champions with each department, obtains permission before publishing a person's name, profile photo, summary, or contact route, and updates office hours and Last verified monthly and whenever assignments change. Use person fields for real tenant accounts and approved organizational contact links; do not invent people or publish personal phone numbers.

program.title: Program Governance - delivery and operations
program.intro: This is the CoE delivery team's restricted workroom: plan an authorized rollout, confirm release readiness, prepare training, coordinate support, and take unresolved policy or funding questions to the proper authority. It is not another policy-making committee or a place for individual student records. The documents below are substantive illustrative drafts for {{OrgName}} review, not adopted procedures or evidence of completed work.

ownerChecklist.title: Approved-member launch checklist
ownerChecklist.intro: These setup steps are kept in the allowlisted Program Governance workroom, so they do not appear on the CoE pages. Only people listed as SharedChannelOwnerUPN or GovernanceAdditionalAllowedMembers can access this channel. Finish the steps before inviting the wider audience. Each one is changed in the organization folder (Deployment-Settings.json or a Content override) and published with 03_Update-CoEContent.ps1.

items.action: Set Links.ServiceDesk to the real approved IT support endpoint. Test it as a non-owner and keep it distinct from incident reporting. Do not invent a ticket category.

Replace sample SupportEmail with the real monitored CoE mailbox, confirm who handles ordinary requests, and confirm response times and service hours before launch. Verify every email link; an unconfigured or sample address is not a live support route.

Set Links.DataSafetyIncident to the organization's real approved incident reporting endpoint, separately from Links.ServiceDesk. Confirm receiving responsibility, confidentiality, access and escalation before launch. No mandatory ticket category is implied. Test this route on Governance, Service Catalog, Give Feedback, Feedback and Roadmap, Start in 10 minutes and Is this OK. If absent, keep the visible route-not-configured caution and do not treat the internal Get Help fallback as a submitted incident.

Set Links.TechnologyRequest to the real approved technology request endpoint, confirm the approval authority and access, and test the route as a non-owner before launch. A missing link does not authorize purchase, installation or agent deployment.

Set Links.AIGuidelines to the organization's actual approved AI guidance. Verify the policy owner, adoption status and access before launch; starter examples and a not-configured link are not adopted policy.
Open every published policy link and hosted document yourself, including PDFs, and confirm each one loads for a non-member account.

Confirm where each roadmap document came from and who may see it. Microsoft roadmap briefings are often under NDA even without markings; keep those in Leadership Governance, not in the public Roadmap folder.

Confirm which Microsoft 365 apps show Copilot Chat and what Copilot Chat in Outlook can reach for unlicensed users (check the Message center), and make the Start in 10 minutes and Who gets what guides, the FAQ, and the Governance page match.
Confirm the informational comparison of Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot with the organization's current entitlements and approved support path.
State whether Study and Learn is the default Copilot experience for students.
Record the owner, completion date, and evidence for each step in this channel before the release gate.
Confirm the agent tiers and the approval route in Leadership Governance before announcing agent building.

Decide whether pay-as-you-go (metered) billing is enabled for agents. Without it, Copilot Chat users can't use agents grounded on SharePoint or other organizational content, so the agent tiers and examples must say so.

Confirm native content approval and draft visibility in the Copilot Agent Showcase list before launch. Review proposals and evidence, mark selected entries Featured before approval if appropriate, then select Approve for ready non-retired entries. Approval is the only publication gate, including edits and retirement. Test with a reader account: pending revisions retain the last approved version, and an approved retirement removes the entry. Seed proposals only; do not autoapprove or create fake approved or Featured test agents.

Confirm native content approval and draft visibility in the Copilot Success Stories list before launch. Keep active submissions Status Submitted and select Approve after content, consent, captions, evidence and video permissions are reviewed; legacy Published remains compatible, not a second publication gate. Revisions and Status Retired also require approval. Test with a reader account that pending revisions show the last approved version and approved retirement removes it. Starter stories remain unapproved drafts without claimed savings. Host no MOCK files, and do not expose draft videos through broadly shared folders.
Choose the tasks, owners, and targets with Leadership Governance before reporting any result.
Replace the starter answers with organization-approved guidance (Content\Copilot-FAQs.md).

The list is filled from the OrgPrompts CSV files (the environment's base set plus any files in Content\OrgPrompts). Upload the same CSV files in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Copilot > Prompts > Import) if you publish organization prompts there, so both places match. Prompts people add on the site wait in the Review view until a catalog reviewer approves them.

The installer does not invite users or assign roles. Name the approved owners and contacts on the page and confirm governance-channel membership before inviting the wider audience. Use a shared-channel owner account whose display name is suitable for a customer walkthrough (SharedChannelOwnerUPN).
Confirm the unit names with the academic affairs office, appoint a primary and backup champion for each unit, fill Last verified, and remove units that do not apply.
Name who refreshes the prompts of the week each semester and who sends champion recognition, and set up the private champions space the guide names before appointing champions.

Ask the information security team to confirm the data levels and every data-level tag on the Prompt library, Start in 10 minutes, the Is this OK check, and any champions material before launch, so the tags carry the organization's authority.

Replace the example data levels and common-case ratings with the organization's own. Confirm Links.AIGuidelines, Links.ServiceDesk, Links.TechnologyRequest and the separate Links.DataSafetyIncident in Deployment-Settings.json, and test configured and route-not-configured journeys without submitting real incidents.

Have academic affairs and HR review the answers about jobs, academic integrity, AI detection, and accessibility before publishing; these are the answers most likely to be read as an organizational position. Confirm the list of supported and unsupported AI tools matches the organization's current guidance.
Name a fluent reviewer for any notice translated with Copilot before it is published.

Assign actual learning owners and reviewers, then record real reviewedOn dates after checking each resource, practice task, access requirement and local guidance. Leave unknown owner and review fields blank until confirmed; never seed an invented owner or review. Verify Microsoft 365 Copilot training URLs and Clipchamp video documentation, and preserve the seven existing prompt headings used by practice anchors.
Replace the DRAFT - DEMONSTRATION sessions with scheduled sessions, or delete them.
Open the Learning Series and confirm the sessions show the intended local time (TimeZone in Deployment-Settings.json sets the site's regional settings).

Launch only after real SupportEmail, Links.ServiceDesk, Links.TechnologyRequest, Links.AIGuidelines and Links.DataSafetyIncident are confirmed; learning ownership and actual reviews are recorded; and agent/story approval and reader-visibility checks pass. Verify every published route and file as a non-owner. Keep sample notices while content is unapproved or launch prerequisites are unresolved. When content and launch are approved, set SampleNotice to none and run 03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -Scope All (Installation Runbook section 6.7).

sections.title: Delivery charter and responsibilities
sections.text: Defines the program lead, IT implementation lead, training lead, and service liaison; separates coordination from academic, privacy, security, and purchasing authority; walks through a request from intake to the authorized decision-maker.

sections.title: 90-day rollout and release gates
sections.text: A relative-week rollout plan with permission and denied-access checks, accessible training, source verification, support handoff, launch prerequisites, and pause criteria. It does not claim a pilot has been authorized.

sections.title: Operational risks and worked issue responses
sections.text: Four fictional cases cover unexpected document discovery, an invented registration deadline, a keyboard-access barrier, and pressure to enable an unreviewed connector. Each identifies the responsible function, containment, and the decision required.

sections.title: Champion and training operating playbook
sections.text: Sets peer-coaching boundaries, safe exercise design, faculty course-rule checks, accessible participation, and the six draft October-December training topics. No real champion appointment or meeting is implied.

sections.title: Support, incidents, and controlled changes
sections.text: Distinguishes ordinary support from product feedback and privacy/security incidents; defines review before new agents, connectors, searches, or data use; specifies access tests, rollback, and evidence needed to resume.

sections.title: Delivery review and action follow-through
sections.text: A proposed weekly working review and monthly leadership handoff, with fictional worked actions and escalation examples. Completion requires evidence; a meeting or assigned action is not an approval.

leadership.title: Leadership Governance - policy, risk, and resources
leadership.intro: This restricted workroom supports institution-level choices: which AI uses are acceptable, who can authorize them, what protections apply, how resources are allocated, and what evidence justifies continuation. Academic, IT, data-steward, privacy, accessibility, and purchasing authorities retain their decision rights. Every document here is an illustrative {{OrgName}} review draft, not adopted policy.

sections.title: AI governance charter and decision authority
sections.text: Defines reserved academic decisions, data-use authorization, technical acceptance, purchasing authority, conditional decisions, and escalation. Coordination or a steering vote cannot override another function's required authorization.

sections.title: First-year AI priorities and selection rules
sections.text: Proposes teaching support, understandable student services, and administrative drafting; includes equitable participation, sequencing, non-AI alternatives, and explicit exclusions for automated consequential decisions.

sections.title: AI acceptable-use and risk decision policy
sections.text: A full draft policy with data-classification boundaries, FERPA-sensitive record controls, human review, course rules, prohibited profiling, a protected-data approval gate, and two fictional worked decisions. The separate {{OrgNoun}}-wide AI policy sets the overarching provisions.

sections.title: Resource allocation, purchase, and renewal rules
sections.text: Defines equitable license allocation, full support and review costs, accessible alternatives, separate spending authority, trial/vendor review, evidence for renewal, and an exit path. Purchase and license quantities are left for the organization to set.

sections.title: Outcomes and honest measurement policy
sections.text: Separates baselines, targets, and actuals; includes concrete sample measures and review effort; prohibits student/employee inference from usage; requires reporting errors, accessibility issues, and limitations alongside benefits.

sections.title: Review, dispositions, and corrective actions
sections.text: Defines proposed participation, required functional determinations, holds, conditional authorization, refusal, suspension, and closure evidence. Two fully worked fictional dispositions demonstrate the procedure without implying organizational decisions.

repairs.topTen: Keep the Top 10 to try label, host the original Microsoft handout in the CoE SharePoint library, and configure the Teams tab for the tenant-hosted file rather than an external download URL. Include an Open in browser fallback.
repairs.remove: Remove the Early Access Program Details control and obsolete EAP links from both the live site and the generated provisioning templates.

deliverables.word: Illustrated implementation guide based on the original HU_MOD Word template, preserving Microsoft branding, David Shih Chun Liu author block, typography, and table of contents.
deliverables.deck: High-level companion PowerPoint explaining each CoE section with clickable live demo links and clearly labelled lab screenshots.
deliverables.scripts: Portable PowerShell reproduction scripts with {{OrgShort}}-specific parameters, safe resume behavior, and access checks; commands and expected results included in the guide.
